main_text.p: [illegible, ~12 letters] potuisse non constitui, vel etiàm e-ius [illegible, ~6 letters] potuisset constitui, posse esse hominibus esse Morale, h. e. commune morum propter Divi-nam [illegible, ~10 letters] ipsis observandorum; & hominibus Naturale, h. e. inde à primâ Natura humanæ origine constitutum, e-umque in conscientia obligans. Vide [illegible, ~8 letters] III. IV, VI.

Qui ego dici deter-minari [illegible, ~10 letters] iuris ipsi Deo [illegible, ~8 letters] ... sed sed so-lum [illegible, ~6 letters] agatur de [illegible, ~8 letters] Divini, non de [illegible, ~6 letters] autem de cultu naturali [illegible, ~6 letters] Quomodo moralem [illegible, ~6 letters] iuris perpetui, [illegible, ~6 letters] Divina? Certè id [illegible, ~8 letters] abuti, eos-[illegible, ~8 letters], & Præceptum [illegible, ~8 letters] quidem sit [illegible, ~8 letters] minùs quàm [illegible, ~8 letters] enim inter moralia [illegible, ~8 letters] est de i-[illegible, ~8 letters] naturali, [illegible, ~8 letters] antiâ?

page.notes: Most of the page is obscured by show-through from the reverse side, and the left part of nearly every line is illegible. Lines were read only where the printed letters are clear; the extent of each gap is estimated. Several words in the middle of lines are doubtful and are not marked individually. The Roman numeral line is partly legible.
